newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - Dec 12.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page Thursday:
- Russia accepted NATO's offer to negotiate a separate formal security relationship with Moscow.

- The U.S. Deprtment of Veterans Affiars acknowledged it waited more than five years to begin major studies on the health effects of exposure to low levels of chemical weapons because of the Pentagon's repeated and inaccurate assurances that there was no evidence that American troops had been exposed to chemical weapons during the Persian Gulf war.

- The U.S. government allowed a former commander in El Salvador's leftist guerrilla army to settle in New Jersey and work as an informant even though officials were convinced he was involved in the killing of six Americans in 1985.

- The Air Force concluded that the general in charge of a military housing complex in Saudi Arabia where 19 Americans were killed in a truck bombing last June took reasonable steps against attack and should not be punished.
- A shipping magnate was confirmed today as China's choice to administer Hong Kong when 150 years of British colonial rule end next July 1.
- The United States all but sealed a deal to liberalize trade in information technology.
- Luxury goods saw sales grow by about 18 percent last year, to $30 billion.
